newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric futures end mixed in narrow trading.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric futures end mixed in narrow trading.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled mixed Wednesday in another light, featureless session despite strength in cash market due to several unplanned plant outages in the western U.S.
The complex tried to extend yesterday's rise, but there was little follow-through buying, brokers and traders said.
"People don't want to get in or out," said a Houston futures trader.
The power contracts did not follow a sharp drop in natural gas futures. The March Henry Hub contract settled down 13.4 cents at $2.090 per million British thermal units.
March California-Oregon Border (COB) futures settled down 15 cents at $10.80 a megawatt hour (MWh) after traded between $10.75 and $10.95. April COB finished down 20 cents at $10.00.
March Palo Verde (PV) futures settled up two cents at $13.24 after bouncing in a 20 cent range. April PV finished up 10 cents at $12.40.
Firm, peak power prices for day-ahead delivery at COB was flat from Tuesday at $12.00-13.50, while those at PV rose $1 to $14.00-15.00
Brokers and traders said they expect the sideway trading to continue barring any inclement weather in the West.
"There is potential for this (complex) to fall, but people are uncomfortable will selling at these levels," the futures trader said.
Separately, restart of a 755 megawatt (MW) unit 4 at the Four Corners coal-fired power plant in New Mexico was pushed back to Thursday after tripping off line Sunday.
A 330 MW unit at the coal-fired Colstrip generating facility near Billings, Montana, was reportedly shut Monday for repairs, and expected to resume operation today.
The 750 MW Navajo coal-fired unit 2 was heard shut Tuesday, and could return to service later this week.
The 1,100 MW pumped storage hydroelectric Helms plant near Fresno, Calif., was shut Feb 1 for mechanical repairs, and could stay down for another week.
NYMEX estimated 170 COB and 204 PV contracts were sold, compared with Tuesday's sales of 231 COB and 88 PV lots.
